rule: Go to your bank branch and ask them to raise your grievance on the Grievance Redressal Module. The SOP expects the bank to submit it within 7 calendar days of your complaint. Also ask the bank for the freeze details: the police station and the case or FIR number and the date of the request and the amount held.

The Kerala High Court has said banks should hold only the disputed amount and not freeze the whole account. It gave this ruling in Dr Sajeer v RBI (judgments of 25 Sept and 6 Oct 2023) and repeated it in later cases.
source: Kerala High Court judgments in Dr Sajeer v RBI as reported by Onmanorama on 19 Oct 2023

rule: The Ministry of Home Affairs SOP dated 2 January 2026 (Clause 10) sets out how account holders can raise grievances. The Grievance Redressal Module has been working since April 2026.
source: MHA SOP dated 02.01.2026 (Clause 10 on page 36); modules live April 2026 per an MHA statement reported by DNA India

rule: On 4 August 2026 the Supreme Court told all States and police to start using the grievance redressal and money restoration modules. It also told the RBI to frame a bank SOP within four weeks.
source: Supreme Court order of 4 Aug 2026 as reported by LiveLaw

rule: If you were scammed, report it immediately on the National Cybercrime Helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in.
source: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal at cybercrime.gov.in and the 1930 helpline

rule: If you let someone else use your account or UPI you may need a lawyer. Call the NALSA helpline 15100 to ask if you qualify for free legal aid. Eligibility depends on your category or income (for example women or SC and ST members or people under a state income limit). Do not claim you are innocent.
Wapas will never ask for money, OTPs, PINs or passwords.
